title: Qualcomm to pay Huawei for first time in 5G, AI patent breakthrough
source_used: Nikkei Asia (opening paragraph, rest paywalled) and tbreak.com (full account citing Reuters, Nikkei, Bloomberg Law, SCMP)
key_facts: Huawei announced on Monday 5 Oct 2026 a cross-licensing agreement with Qualcomm covering 5G and AI technologies (tbreak: also computing and networking).
Nikkei reports Qualcomm would pay to use Huawei patents for the first time and become the net payer once the deal takes effect.
Huawei first paid to license Qualcomm patents in 2001.
Qualcomm will also buy selected Huawei US patents in computing, AI and networking (tbreak, citing Reuters).
The deal needs regulatory approval, including a U.S. review; value and timing were not disclosed.
Bloomberg Law reportedly says the deal covers patents behind Huawei's LogicFolding chipmaking technique.
quote_evidence: Huawei announced Monday that rival mobile chipmaker Qualcomm would pay to use its patents for the first time, in a cross-licensing agreement covering 5G and AI technologies.
The deal marks a breakthrough for the Chinese company's intellectual property portfolio but will trigger a regulatory review in the U.S.
why_it_matters_hint: A U.S. chip giant paying a Chinese rival for patents reverses a 25-year licensing direction, but terms are undisclosed.
notes: Nikkei page mostly paywalled (567 chars); fuller details read at tbreak.com (decoded from Google News), which cites Reuters, Nikkei, Bloomberg Law and SCMP. SCMP and Bloomberg pages blocked.
